question: Why do researchers use statistical tables alongside written text in a report?

options.C: Tables are meant to confuse readers who do not understand math

question: What must be obtained from participants before data collection begins?

question: What is the absolute first thing a nurse checks during an initial trauma assessment?

question: Which of these is a bad practice when looking at clinical data?

question: What happens to disease prevalence if a new, highly effective cure is discovered?

question: How should a nurse verify that a walking cane is fitted correctly for a patient?

options.C: The handle should align with the patient's wrist crease

question: Why does the healthcare team do a home assessment before a patient is discharged?

options.A: It helps identify physical barriers like stairs or narrow doors that could cause falls or limit mobility

options.C: It proves to the doctor that the client no longer needs any assistance

explanation: Checking the home early helps spot hazards like steps or narrow doors so ramps or rails can be fitted before the patient arrives. Safety first! [learn more](GNS314_U5_T2#GNS314_U5_T2_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of using Microsoft PowerPoint in healthcare?

options.A: Tracking daily financial budgets and supply inventories

question: Why is measuring hourly urine output so important when monitoring a bleeding patient?

question: You wear sterile gloves and a mask while putting in a urinary catheter. Which link in the infection chain are you mainly trying to block?

options.A: Reservoir

options.C: Susceptible host
options.D: Infectious agent

explanation: Awesome! Using sterile barriers blocks germs from sneaking into vulnerable places like the urinary tract. [learn more](GST114_U2_T1#GST114_U2_T1_h7)

question: Why does the body quickly develop metabolic acidosis during severe asphyxia?

options.A: Anaerobic metabolism produces excess lactic acid
options.B: Liver cells release stored hydrochloric acid
options.C: Lungs absorb too much environmental nitrogen
options.D: The kidneys stop filtering urea completely

explanation: When cells are starved of oxygen, they switch to emergency backup power (anaerobic metabolism). This backup mode makes energy, but it leaves behind a lot of lactic acid, which makes the blood acidic. Great job reviewing your metabolism basics! [learn more](GNS112_U7_T1#GNS112_U7_T1_h1)

question: Why is Gallows traction only used for babies under two years old?

options.A: Toddlers over two refuse to lie flat
options.B: The straps are just too small for older kids
options.C: Heavier kids can lift their bodies and ruin the pull
options.D: Older children have bones that are too brittle

question: Which principle ensures that vulnerable voices are heard equally during community meetings?

options.A: Competition
options.B: Isolation
options.C: Delegation
options.D: Equity

explanation: Equity focuses on fairness and making sure that everyone, especially the less powerful, gets a chance to speak and participate. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T6#GNS124_U4_T6_h2)

question: What makes the copper IUD special compared to emergency contraceptive pills?

options.A: It is only effective if taken within the first two hours
options.B: It must be swallowed as a tablet with a full glass of water
options.C: It provides ongoing long-term birth control after emergency use
options.D: It permanently stops a woman from ever having children

explanation: The copper IUD is a double-whammy: it works as emergency contraception right now, and it can stay in place to prevent pregnancy for years. Super convenient! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h5)

question: You find an abandoned elderly woman in a village with no food or medical care. What is the best way to coordinate her care?

options.A: Connect her with local social welfare agencies and senior support programs
options.B: Tell her neighbors to handle it completely on their own
options.C: Wait until the federal health budget is reviewed next year
options.D: Admit her to the maternity ward for routine antenatal checks

explanation: You're thinking like a true nurse! Your role includes acting as a bridge, linking vulnerable patients directly to the social services and agencies equipped to help them long-term. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T26#GNS225_U5_T26_h8)

question: You are the first nurse to arrive at an accident scene and you notice a strong smell of leaking gas. What is your very first step?

options.A: Wait inside the ambulance until police complete all paperwork.
options.B: Run immediately to pull victims out of the wreckage.
options.C: Ensure personal safety and environmental security before entering.

explanation: Safety first! If you rush in and become a victim yourself, you can't help anyone. Always check that the environment is safe before stepping in. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T2#GNS315_U1_T2_h2)

question: Why is pulse oximetry sometimes called the fifth vital sign in busy clinical wards?

options.A: It must be recorded before measuring temperature or pulse

options.C: It is checked every five hours on all ward patients

question: What usually happens when a country struggles to collect enough domestic taxes for public services?

options.A: A sudden surplus of funds for hospital construction

options.C: Immediate achievement of the Abuja Declaration target
options.D: Increased reliance on external grants and borrowing

question: How did the invention of psychotropic drugs change the daily job of a psychiatric nurse?

options.A: It shifted their focus from physical containment to rehabilitation and therapy
options.B: It increased the frequency of using physical restraints and seclusion
options.C: It forced nurses to spend most of their shifts performing surgeries
options.D: It eliminated the need for any direct patient interaction or observation

question: A 16-year-old girl drops out of school due to an unplanned pregnancy. What long-term impact is she most likely to face?

options.A: Immediate government employment

question: Why does sensorineural hearing loss often make speech sound muffled instead of just quiet?

options.A: Excess earwax completely fills the inner ear chambers
options.B: The middle ear bones fuse together to block high pitches
options.C: The eardrum becomes too thick to vibrate at any frequency
options.D: Inner ear damage alters how sound clarity and frequencies are processed

explanation: Great job thinking this through! When the inner ear or auditory nerve gets damaged, it messes up how details and frequencies are sent to the brain, turning clear words into a muffled sound. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T7#GNS324_U4_T7_h1)

question: What is the main job of self-tolerance in our immune system?

options.A: To prevent the immune system from attacking healthy body tissue
options.B: To destroy foreign invaders like bacteria and viruses
options.C: To increase the production of red blood cells
options.D: To help white blood cells mature in the lymph nodes

explanation: Think of self-tolerance as the immune system's security check. It helps white blood cells recognize our own body parts so they don't mistakenly attack healthy organs! [learn more](GST114_U4_T8#GST114_U4_T8_h1)

question: Why is good room ventilation a must in spaces where chemical disinfectants like glutaraldehyde are used?

options.A: To prevent toxic vapors from accumulating and harming respiratory tracts

options.C: To speed up the drying time of washed stainless steel basins
options.D: To reduce ambient room humidity so metal instruments do not rust

explanation: These strong chemicals give off fumes that can mess with your lungs if they build up in a closed, stuffy room. Always keep the air moving! [learn more](GST114_U2_T9#GST114_U2_T9_h6)

question: In an emergency, when would a nurse use a defibrillator?

options.A: To slow down a fast heart rate caused by a mild fever
options.B: To restart a heart that already has a normal, healthy rhythm
options.C: To check the electrical resistance of the chest skin
options.D: To stop dangerous, chaotic heart rhythms like ventricular fibrillation

explanation: A defibrillator delivers a quick shock to pause chaotic electrical activity so the heart's natural pacemaker can take over again. Lifesaving nursing knowledge! [learn more](GNS315_U4_T2#GNS315_U4_T2_h2)

question: Why is inflammation affecting any layer of the heart considered a serious medical concern?

options.A: It exclusively affects the lungs and has no impact on circulation
options.B: It only causes temporary skin rashes on the chest wall
options.C: It can severely compromise the heart's ability to pump blood effectively
options.D: It instantly stops all electrical activity without warning

question: Why do nurse researchers set clear objectives when doing explanatory research?

question: Which activity must occur before an HIV test is administered to a client?

question: Why do negative feedback loops usually fail when a gland is overproducing hormones?

question: What is a major ethical puzzle that community health nurses face more often than hospital nurses?

question: A state ministry of health hires a private company to handle medical waste for all public hospitals. What is this called?

question: What is the correct sequence when putting on personal protective equipment before entering an isolation room?

question: Why do large, complex proteins usually make much better antigens than small, simple molecules?

question: Why do nurse researchers study a smaller sample instead of the whole population?

question: Which sign is commonly seen in school-aged children with an undiagnosed learning disability?

question: Which signs are classic for a life-threatening thyroid storm?

question: What is the primary hormone responsible for moving glucose from the bloodstream into body cells?

question: Why does milk make it so easy for bacteria to grow quickly?

question: At what capacity should a waste bag be securely closed and removed?

question: What usually happens when a hospital runs on a strict blame culture?

question: What daily habit is most important for a patient with heart failure to spot early fluid buildup?

question: How do modern nursing training programs differ from the older styles?

question: How do bedside nurses play a direct role in improving healthcare quality?

question: During a weaning trial, which sign tells you that the patient is struggling and needs ventilator support put back on?

question: Which of these is NOT a normal benefit of well-funded disease-specific health programs?

question: Why is 'system interoperability' such a big deal when hospitals share patient records?

question: In infection control, what do we call a non-living object like a stethoscope or door handle that can pass germs from one person to another?

question: A patient is prescribed a sustained-release capsule for chronic pain. What must the nurse tell the patient about taking this medication?

question: During heavy rainfall, animal waste and fertilizers wash off a massive grazing field into a nearby river. What type of pollution source is this?

question: When hospital managers look at research findings, what information do they care about the most?

question: A hospital encourages nurses to log medication errors openly so the team can review them. Which core component does this action demonstrate?

question: What is the main reason we use the coefficient of variation in research?

question: Why do doctors sometimes order a contrast angiogram for someone with severe peripheral vascular disease?

options.C: To see if the patient has high blood pressure overall

question: Why do blood disorders like sickle cell anaemia often cause deep emotional distress for patients?

options.C: Because patients get a quick and complete cure in most hospitals

question: What should you check first if a patient with a catheter suddenly stops passing urine?

question: A patient is feeling like giving up after a small setback in their recovery. What is the best way to help them build resilience?

question: A lab machine sends blood test results straight into a patient's electronic chart without losing data. What makes this smooth transfer possible?

question: What should you do with a used needle right after giving an injection?

question: How can Nigeria best achieve long-term financial sustainability for its health care system?

options.D: Estrogen causes the kidneys to excrete all dietary calcium

explanation: Estrogen acts like a shield for bones by slowing down bone breakdown. Without it, bones can lose their density faster. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T15#GNS121_U5_T15_h7)

question: Why do nurses need to understand health care costs?

options.A: To diagnose complex financial diseases in the community
options.B: To calculate daily profits for the hospital pharmacy
options.C: To help patients navigate financial strain and advocate for them
options.D: To replace hospital accountants during budget reviews

explanation: You will often see how money worries affect your patients. Knowing about healthcare costs helps you support and speak up for them when they face tough financial choices. [learn more](GST322_U2_T1#GST322_U2_T1_h1)

question: What does the term "not-invented-here syndrome" mean in a hospital setting?

options.A: Staff reject a new practice simply because they did not come up with it themselves
options.B: Nurses refuse to care for patients admitted from another hospital
options.C: Management bans any new clinical guidelines written by outside experts
options.D: The hospital refuses to buy medical equipment made in foreign countries

explanation: Have you ever seen people reject a good idea just because it wasn't their own? That's 'not-invented-here syndrome'—a common human habit we learn to overcome! [learn more](GST319_U1_T6#GST319_U1_T6_h3)

question: By what age does a typical infant double their birth weight?

options.A: Six months
options.B: Nine months
options.C: Three months
options.D: Twelve months

explanation: Infants generally double their birth weight by six months of age and triple it by twelve months. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T12#GNS324_U3_T12_h2)

question: What makes NGOs so helpful when it comes to community food projects?

options.A: They possess unlimited financial budgets compared to national governments.
options.B: They rely exclusively on military force to secure food warehouses.
options.C: They can reach remote or marginalized populations that large governments often miss.
options.D: They have legal authority to write and pass new national laws.

explanation: Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs) are flexible and grassroots, meaning they can travel to tiny, hard-to-reach villages where big government programs rarely go. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T029#GNS227_U2_T029_h4)

question: When an IT committee is choosing computers for an outpatient clinic, what should guide their choice?

options.A: Matching the device processing capability to daily clinical workflow needs
options.B: Purchasing the largest supercomputers available on the market
options.C: Selecting analog hardware to measure physical wave signals
options.D: Choosing the most expensive mainframe system for single-user desks

explanation: You got it! The best approach is always matching the tool to the actual daily job, saving money and keeping nurses smiling. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T6#GNS113_U1_T6_h7)

question: What is the main duty of NAFDAC regarding medications?

options.A: Providing free meals to hospitalized patients
options.B: Regulating drug manufacturing, importation, and quality
options.C: Issuing practicing licenses to individual bedside nurses
options.D: Managing the internal budget of teaching hospitals

explanation: NAFDAC ensures that all drugs sold or used in the country are safe, effective, and of good quality. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T13#GNS122_U1_T13_h3)

question: What is the recommended class of drugs for treating uncomplicated malaria?

options.A: Artemisinin-based combination therapies
options.B: Long-acting sulfonamide antibiotics
options.C: Topical antifungal creams
options.D: Single-agent chloroquine tablets

explanation: Artemisinin-based combinations (ACTs) are the gold standard because they clear the malaria parasite quickly and help prevent drug resistance. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T6#GNS215_U6_T6_h4)

question: Which electrolyte is found mostly inside the cells and is vital for heart rhythm?

options.A: Potassium
options.B: Calcium
options.C: Sodium
options.D: Chloride

explanation: Potassium is the chief intracellular cation, and even small changes in its level can dangerously disrupt heart rhythm. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T7#GNS123_U3_T7_h3)

question: Poor waste disposal and unsafe drinking water lead directly to which group of diseases?

options.A: Genetic blood disorders like sickle cell anemia
options.B: Fecal-oral diseases like cholera and typhoid
options.C: Airborne infections like tuberculosis
options.D: Sexually transmitted infections

explanation: You got it! When sanitation fails, germs from human waste easily find their way into drinking water, spreading nasty tummy bugs. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T16#GNS313_U1_T16_h6)

question: What major historical event drove Florence Nightingale to collect and analyze health data?

options.A: The American Civil War
options.B: The Crimean War
options.C: World War I
options.D: The 1918 Influenza Pandemic

explanation: Nightingale systematically tracked illness and death rates among wounded soldiers during her service in the Crimean War to prove the value of hospital sanitation. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T3#GNS217_U2_T3_h1)

question: Why is it important for nurses to review immunization registers regularly?

options.A: To calculate monthly staff salary and allowances
options.B: To identify children who have missed scheduled doses and need tracking
options.C: To find out which vaccine brand is most expensive
options.D: To report families to local law enforcement authorities

explanation: Regular register checks help nurses spot missing children early so they can organize follow-up visits before outbreaks happen. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T71#GNS214_U1_T71_h6)

question: What does it mean to confuse correlation with causation in healthcare?

options.A: Assuming one event caused another just because they happened together
options.B: Failing to record patient vital signs in the electronic health record
options.C: Comparing infection rates between two completely different hospitals
options.D: Using the wrong chart type to present monthly admission numbers

explanation: Spot on! Just because two things happen at the same time doesn't mean one caused the other. Always dig deeper! [learn more](GST319_U1_T2#GST319_U1_T2_h5)

question: Why is strict adherence especially important when taking antibiotics or antiretroviral drugs?

options.A: To eliminate the need for any future medical checkups
options.B: To ensure the medication tastes better to the patient
options.C: To speed up how quickly the drug is excreted by the kidneys
options.D: To prevent the development of drug-resistant strains of infections

explanation: Missing doses of anti-infective drugs allows surviving microorganisms to mutate and resist the medication, rendering future treatments ineffective. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T2#GNS215_U4_T2_h2)

question: What is the medical and event term for the phase when a crowd is arriving at a venue?

options.A: Ingress
options.B: Triage
options.C: Egress
options.D: Dispersion

explanation: Remember: Ingress means going in (arriving), while egress means exiting (leaving). Easy to mix up, but you've got this! [learn more](GNS315_U3_T3#GNS315_U3_T3_h4)

question: Which Nigerian legislation sets the legal age of marriage at eighteen years?

options.A: The National Health Act
options.B: The Penal Code Act
options.C: The Child Rights Act
options.D: The Matrimonial Causes Decree

explanation: The Child Rights Act explicitly defines a child as anyone under 18 and prohibits marriage at that age. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T9#GNS312_U1_T9_h7)

question: What does a cracking or grating sound in a joint (called crepitus) usually mean?

options.A: Rapid healing of a fracture through callus tissue
options.B: Rough bone ends grinding against each other
options.C: Excessive accumulation of healthy synovial fluid
options.D: Normal sliding of smooth articular cartilage

explanation: Crepitus is that crunching feeling you get when the smooth cartilage is gone and bare bones scrape together during movement. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T20#GNS222_U1_T20_h6)

question: Why must on-site spotters communicate with the command center so quickly?

options.A: To allow rapid intervention before minor crowding turns into a crisis
options.B: To ensure ticket sales data is updated every minute
options.C: To prevent performers from starting their show too early
options.D: To coordinate food delivery schedules for vendors

explanation: Spotting a bottleneck early and radioing the team straight away can stop a small crowd crush before it ever starts. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T3#GNS315_U3_T3_h5)

question: Why do we put healthy-feeling people into quarantine after a known exposure to a contagious illness?

options.A: To monitor them through the incubation period before they can spread the disease asymptomatically
options.B: To punish individuals who failed to maintain proper personal hygiene standards
options.C: To immediately administer therapeutic antibiotics regardless of the actual pathogen involved
options.D: To provide them with active immunity through immediate vaccination in a controlled facility

explanation: Spot on! It catches sneaky infections early so they don't pass them on to others before showing symptoms. [learn more](GST114_U2_T5#GST114_U2_T5_h7)

question: A client looks in the mirror after an EEG and feels upset because their hair is messy with sticky paste. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Help the client wash their hair with warm water and shampoo
options.B: Ask the physician to write an order for a scalp scrub
options.C: Apply rubbing alcohol to dissolve the paste quickly
options.D: Tell the client the paste will wash off on its own tomorrow

explanation: That electrode paste can be super sticky and stubborn! Helping the patient clean up shows great bedside manner and restores their comfort. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T9#GNS222_U3_T9_h5)

question: When must a nurse choose soap and water instead of an alcohol hand rub?

options.A: Before touching a patient who has intact skin
options.B: When hands are visibly soiled with dirt or body fluids
options.C: When entering a clean general medical ward
options.D: After taking a patient's temperature with a digital thermometer

explanation: Spot on! Alcohol rubs are great, but they can't wash away physical dirt. When your hands look or feel dirty, good old soap and water is a must. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T9#GNS313_U2_T9_h2)

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard security measure used to protect electronic patient records?

options.A: Publicly posting patient medical histories on hospital hallway notice boards
options.B: Password protection and secure login credentials for every clinician
options.C: Biometric fingerprint scanners to verify staff identity at the workstation
options.D: Role-based access controls that limit file viewing to authorized staff

explanation: Posting private health information publicly violates core confidentiality principles and patient privacy laws. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h6)

question: When getting informed consent from a patient for a research study, which of these actions is completely unacceptable?

options.A: Threatening to withhold routine nursing care if the patient refuses to join
options.B: Explaining both the potential risks and benefits of the study clearly
options.C: Ensuring the patient knows they can withdraw at any time without penalty
options.D: Allowing adequate time for the patient to ask questions about the project

explanation: Research participation must always be 100% voluntary. You can never use basic patient care as a weapon or a tool for coercion! [learn more](GNS224_U1_T4#GNS224_U1_T4_h7)

question: Why is the nurse-resident relationship in long-term care so special compared to acute care?

options.A: Family members take over all nursing responsibilities
options.B: Extended stay allows for deeper therapeutic relationships
options.C: Short patient stays prevent any meaningful connections
options.D: Nurses only interact with residents during medication passes

explanation: Spot on! Because residents live there for months or years, you really get to know them and their families, which helps you notice even the smallest changes in their health. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T9#GNS324_U5_T9_h2)

question: How is formal nursing research different from just guessing or solving a ward problem on the spot?

options.A: Research follows a structured and disciplined pathway
options.B: Research never involves human participants
options.C: Research is always performed by doctors alone
options.D: Casual problem-solving uses more statistics

explanation: Spot on! While we solve ward problems every day, formal research follows careful, step-by-step rules to make sure the answers are truly reliable. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T1#GNS217_U2_T1_h1)

question: Which of these is a dangerous mistake during an emergency obstetric triage?

options.A: Notifying the medical doctor immediately upon finding abnormal bleeding
options.B: Placing an unstable patient in a quiet resuscitation bay
options.C: Delaying vital sign assessment to fill out admission paperwork
options.D: Checking maternal blood pressure upon entry

explanation: Never let paperwork delay patient care! In emergencies, checking vital signs and stabilizing the patient comes first. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T009#GNS226_U1_T009_h5)

question: Why is community diagnosis performed during mobilisation?

options.A: To test every resident for rare genetic disorders
options.B: To collect money from villagers for the clinic roof
options.C: To identify major local health problems and priorities together
options.D: To decide which nurses will be transferred

explanation: Community diagnosis helps health workers and residents discover what health issues matter most to the locals. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T2#GNS124_U4_T2_h5)

question: How does cultural stigma affect the two-way referral process?

options.A: It ensures that primary health clinics receive adequate funding from local chiefs
options.B: It delays initial professional help-seeking, often bringing clients to the hospital only in severe crises
options.C: It makes downward referral unnecessary because clients recover faster at home
options.D: It encourages families to maintain smooth communication with tertiary psychiatrists

explanation: Because of stigma, families often try other options first. By the time they reach the hospital, the illness has usually progressed to a crisis. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T4#GNS314_U4_T4_h6)

question: What is a major perk of getting your vitamins from real food instead of pills?

options.A: Pills are always completely fake and contain no actual vitamins
options.B: Whole foods provide fiber and a complex nutritional matrix
options.C: Whole foods cost nothing at all to produce or purchase
options.D: Pills take up to a week to dissolve in the human stomach

explanation: Spot on! Whole foods come with extra bonuses like fiber and natural plant compounds that supplements just can't copy. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T004#GNS227_U2_T004_h3)

question: Who is most likely to act as the primary day-to-day caregiver for a patient recovering at home?

options.A: Family members living with or near the client
options.B: The contracted medical equipment delivery driver
options.C: Voluntary auditors from the federal government
options.D: The regional health commissioner on duty

explanation: That's right! In our setting, family is everything. Loved ones usually do the heavy lifting of supporting patients between our visits. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T1#GNS324_U2_T1_h3)

question: A patient is admitted with sudden, severe confusion and mood swings. What must the nurse consider first based on biological etiology?

options.A: Whether an underlying physical illness or hormone imbalance is causing the symptoms
options.B: How long the patient has been using herbal sleeping mixtures
options.C: Which family member caused the patient to feel stressed recently
options.D: If the patient experienced a difficult childhood in the village

explanation: Medical issues like thyroid problems or infections can cause psychiatric symptoms, so biological causes must be investigated during assessment. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T4#GNS314_U2_T4_h2)

question: Why should a nurse explain neurological tests using simple, non-medical terms?

options.A: To shorten the overall duration of the hospital stay
options.B: To reduce patient anxiety and improve cooperation
options.C: To replace the need for a physical examination
options.D: To avoid documenting the assessment in the medical record

explanation: Clear and simple communication helps calm the patient so they can participate fully and accurately in the assessment. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T1#GNS221_U2_T1_h2)

question: How do thorough tracking records help healthcare facility managers over time?

options.A: They allow the hospital to fine clients who miss clinic days
options.B: They highlight recurring community barriers and help improve service delivery
options.C: They ensure that nurses never have to talk to clients directly
options.D: They eliminate all paperwork from the nursing station

explanation: When we track patterns, managers can spot common roadblocks—like transport challenges or drug stockouts—and fix them for everyone! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T025#GNS226_U6_T025_h7)

question: Why is it important to involve local leaders right from the start of a health project?

options.A: It builds a sense of ownership and encourages community cooperation
options.B: It ensures that only the wealthiest families get treated
options.C: It stops the community from asking questions
options.D: It prevents nurses from having to do any work at all

explanation: When leaders feel involved from day one, they champion the project themselves, leading to wonderful community trust and success! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T8#GNS124_U5_T8_h6)

question: What often happens when patients simply cannot afford the high cost of their prescribed medications?

options.A: Pharmacies are forced to give all drugs away
options.B: They may skip doses or stop taking them
options.C: Hospital admissions instantly drop to zero
options.D: They automatically receive free government refills

explanation: Exactly. When out-of-pocket costs are too high, patients often try to stretch their drugs by skipping doses, which delays their healing. [learn more](GST322_U5_T1#GST322_U5_T1_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of an Electronic Health Record (EHR)?

options.A: To store health insurance billing information for government agencies
options.B: To replace traditional bedside nursing care with automated tasks
options.C: To store a patient's digital medical history for authorized sharing
options.D: To provide patients with a private diary of their daily symptoms

explanation: An EHR is a digital chart designed primarily to collect and safely share comprehensive patient health information among healthcare providers. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h1)

question: What exactly is a 'sampling frame' in research?

options.A: The final group of patients selected for a clinical trial
options.B: The statistical formula used to calculate sample size
options.C: A physical list of all eligible members in a target population
options.D: A barrier preventing patients from joining a study

explanation: You got it! Think of the sampling frame as your actual register, directory, or database from which you pull your participants. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T18#GNS224_U1_T18_h2)

question: Why was developing pure culture techniques a massive breakthrough for microbiology?

options.A: It eliminated the need for any form of physical handwashing in clinics
options.B: It enabled doctors to cure viral infections using heavy metal solutions
options.C: It proved conclusively that animals could generate spontaneous life in mud
options.D: It allowed researchers to grow and study one single type of microorganism at a time

explanation: Before this, samples were mixed and confusing. Growing one species at a time let scientists study specific germs clearly. [learn more](GST114_U1_T2#GST114_U1_T2_h3)

question: Which of these is a great example of cost-effective healthcare planning?

options.A: Purchasing expensive imported machines instead of servicing local ones
options.B: Waiting until patients are critically ill before treating them
options.C: Focusing heavily on preventive health education in the community
options.D: Throwing away opened medication vials at the end of every shift

explanation: Brilliant! Stopping a disease before it starts is always much cheaper and easier than treating late-stage sickness. [learn more](GST322_U5_T5#GST322_U5_T5_h5)

question: What role does the community health nurse play during participatory community diagnosis?

options.A: A politician who promises free money for everyone
options.B: A facilitator who guides and works alongside the community
options.C: A distant observer who never talks to local residents
options.D: A strict commander who gives orders without explanation

explanation: Nurses work collaboratively with local people to empower them rather than imposing solutions from above. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T3#GNS124_U3_T3_h4)

question: Why must nurses in Nigeria ask patients about traditional herbs or local concoctions during a drug history check?

options.A: Local herbs replace the need for checking kidney function tests.
options.B: Traditional mixtures are always completely harmless and speed up healing.
options.C: Herbs can interact with prescription drugs and cause unexpected adverse reactions.
options.D: Hospitals require herbal documentation to qualify for government funding.

explanation: Patients often use local herbs alongside hospital medications. Knowing about them helps us catch and prevent dangerous drug-herb clashes! [learn more](GNS125_U5_T8#GNS125_U5_T8_h6)

question: A student nurse checks a drug's mechanism and possible side effects before giving it to a patient. Which historical role of nursing does this action reflect?

options.A: The nurse performing duties restricted only to senior physicians
options.B: The nurse relying solely on oral traditional folklore
options.C: The nurse acting as a primitive apothecary mixer from the Middle Ages
options.D: The nurse acting as an active safety barrier and clinical monitor

explanation: Modern nurses serve as the final safety check in medication administration, requiring them to understand drug actions and watch for adverse reactions before and after giving medication. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T1#GNS125_U1_T1_h6)

question: In Vroom's expectancy theory, what does 'expectancy' actually mean?

options.A: The fear of being punished for a clinical error
options.B: The financial value attached to a year-end bonus
options.C: The belief that effort will lead to successful performance
options.D: The strict rules enforced by the hospital director

explanation: Correct! Expectancy is your personal belief that if you work hard, you will actually succeed at the task. [learn more](GST321_U3_T5#GST321_U3_T5_h5)

question: What is the difference between a key driver and a change idea?

options.A: Drivers deal only with financial costs, while change ideas deal with clinical medications
options.B: Drivers are primary systems influencing the outcome, while change ideas are specific practical actions to test
options.C: Drivers are chosen by hospital directors, while change ideas are chosen by patients
options.D: Drivers are written on paper, while change ideas are only spoken aloud

explanation: Think of drivers as the big areas we need to influence, while change ideas are the fun, practical steps we actually try out on the ward! [learn more](GST319_U3_T1#GST319_U3_T1_h3)

question: What is a simple way nurses can help reduce the emotional burden of isolation?

options.A: Reduce nursing visits so the patient can rest in peace
options.B: Leave the isolation door wide open so the patient can watch the hallway
options.C: Spend time talking with the patient and use video calls to connect with family
options.D: Tell the patient not to worry because isolation is not a big deal

explanation: Active communication and helping the patient stay in touch with loved ones greatly reduces feelings of isolation and depression. [learn more](GST114_U2_T17#GST114_U2_T17_h7)

question: How is a wheat allergy different from celiac disease?

options.A: Wheat allergy involves IgE antibody responses rather than autoimmune villous atrophy
options.B: Celiac disease symptoms only appear after age fifty
options.C: Wheat allergy causes permanent damage to the liver instead of the gut
options.D: Celiac disease is caused by a bacterial infection of the stomach

explanation: A wheat allergy is a classic immune system allergic reaction (using IgE antibodies), whereas celiac disease is an autoimmune condition that specifically harms the gut lining. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T011#GNS227_U6_T011_h2)

question: A patient with a tracheostomy suddenly struggles to breathe, turns bluish, and you can't pass a suction catheter down the tube. What is likely happening?

options.A: Normal post-operative recovery
options.B: A mucous plug blocking the airway
options.C: The cuff is completely deflated
options.D: The oxygen flow rate is too high

explanation: If your catheter won't go through and the patient is in distress, a thick mucous plug is usually blocking the pipe. This is an urgent call for action! [learn more](GNS315_U4_T1#GNS315_U4_T1_h6)

question: Which cells are the star players in our adaptive (targeted) immune response?

options.A: Adipocytes
options.B: Platelets
options.C: Lymphocytes
options.D: Erythrocytes

explanation: B cells and T cells are types of lymphocytes. They are the smart cells that handle the targeted, long-term memory side of immunity. [learn more](GST114_U4_T6#GST114_U4_T6_h3)

question: Why is emotional and psychological support so important for patients in skin traction?

options.A: Mental fatigue prevents the patient from eating hospital meals
options.B: Anxious patients have higher rates of bone infection than calm ones
options.C: Psychological stress stops the traction weights from pulling correctly
options.D: Bed confinement and restricted movement cause significant anxiety and frustration

explanation: Being stuck flat in one position is tough on the mind as well as the body. A kind word and clear communication go a long way in nursing care! [learn more](GNS221_U1_T8#GNS221_U1_T8_h7)

question: What is the big benefit of the healthcare team using the same diagnostic terms?

options.A: It reduces the total cost of hospital administration
options.B: It allows clear communication and predictable care planning
options.C: It ensures patients never experience adverse drug reactions
options.D: It removes all personal bias from psychiatric nursing

explanation: When everyone on the ward speaks the same clinical language, patient handovers become smooth and clear. Great job thinking like a nurse! [learn more](GNS314_U2_T3#GNS314_U2_T3_h1)

question: Why do social factors like poverty play such a big role in NCDs?

options.A: They ensure that patients always adhere strictly to their medication regimen
options.B: They directly cause genetic mutations that trigger cancer within weeks
options.C: They limit access to healthy foods, safe exercise spaces, and proper healthcare
options.D: They completely eliminate the risk of developing infectious diseases

explanation: Exactly! When money is tight, it becomes much harder to afford nutritious food, find safe places to exercise, or visit the clinic early for check-ups. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T1#GNS313_U3_T1_h2)

question: Why is the time right after breakfast often the best time to try having a bowel movement?

options.A: Stomach acid levels are at their lowest point of the day
options.B: Blood pressure peaks and helps push waste forward
options.C: Eating food triggers a natural wave of activity in the colon
options.D: Digestive enzymes are most active in the rectum then

explanation: Eating stimulates the gastrocolic reflex, which increases muscle contractions in the colon and creates a natural urge to go. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T6#GNS212_U1_T6_h6)

question: Why is it so helpful for a recovering patient to talk to another person who has also gone through an amputation?

options.A: It stops the patient from ever experiencing phantom limb pain again.
options.B: It gives practical proof that a fulfilling life and independence are possible.
options.C: Friends who share the same diagnosis speed up physical wound healing.
options.D: Peer visitors are trained medical professionals who can change dressings.

explanation: Seeing someone else thrive after the same experience gives wonderful hope and makes the patient feel much less alone. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T12#GNS324_U4_T12_h7)

question: A scared patient asks if the metal pins will hurt going into their head. What should you say?

options.A: You will feel a sharp pain, but it will go away as soon as the weights are hung.
options.B: Do not worry, the pins are very small and just rest on top of your hair.
options.C: Most patients are asleep during the whole process so they never feel anything.
options.D: The doctor will numb your scalp with medicine first so you won't feel sharp pain.

explanation: Always be honest and comforting! Letting them know the doctor will numb the area first builds great trust and calms their nerves. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T11#GNS221_U1_T11_h4)

question: What is the main goal of building a safety culture in a hospital?

options.A: Ensuring hospitals meet strict financial profit margins
options.B: Reducing the total number of employed nursing personnel
options.C: Prioritizing patient protection from accidental harm above all else
options.D: Punishing staff members who make clinical errors

explanation: Spot on! A safety culture is all about putting patient safety first and making sure everyone works together to prevent accidental harm. [learn more](GST319_U5_T3#GST319_U5_T3_h1)

question: Why do we use an interdisciplinary team in palliative care?

options.A: It reduces the total number of staff members needed in a hospital
options.B: It covers the diverse physical, emotional, and spiritual needs of the patient
options.C: It prevents families from speaking with the healthcare team
options.D: It ensures that doctors make all decisions without consulting others

explanation: Fantastic! Because end-of-life care touches every part of a person's life, it takes a diverse team of experts to cover all their physical, emotional, and spiritual needs. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T3#GNS321_U4_T3_h7)

question: Why do patients often forget to mention herbal supplements when you ask about their medications?

options.A: Supplements never interact with prescription medications
options.B: Pharmacists automatically upload supplement lists to charts
options.C: Federal laws prohibit patients from discussing herbs in hospitals
options.D: They do not consider supplements to be real medicine

explanation: You got it! Because herbs and vitamins are bought over-the-counter, patients often don't think to mention them, even though they can interact with drugs. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T3#GNS222_U3_T3_h5)

question: What made the Aro village psychiatric system, created by Dr. T. Adeoye Lambo, so special?

options.A: It replaced all psychiatric medications with traditional herbal mixtures
options.B: It integrated families and local communities into the patient's treatment process
options.C: It moved all mental health care services exclusively into high-rise city hospitals
options.D: It isolated patients entirely from their relatives to speed up recovery

explanation: Lambo's village model was brilliant! It respected local culture and brought families straight into the healing journey, blending hospital care with normal community life. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T4#GNS314_U1_T4_h7)

question: A nurse notices a patient coughing and clearing their throat repeatedly while eating a soft meal. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Give the patient a dry biscuit to clear the throat
options.B: Document that the meal was 100 percent eaten
options.C: Stop the meal immediately and assess breathing
options.D: Encourage the patient to eat faster to finish

explanation: Coughing during meals is a primary warning sign of aspiration or swallowing difficulty, requiring an immediate pause in feeding. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T002#GNS227_U6_T002_h7)

question: A care assistant is about to feed a resident who has trouble swallowing. What safety tip should you give?

options.A: Offer large chunks of solid food for better chewing
options.B: Feed the resident as quickly as possible
options.C: Position the resident in an upright sitting posture
options.D: Encourage the resident to lie flat on the bed

explanation: Brilliant! Sitting upright uses gravity to help swallowing and keeps food out of the lungs, preventing dangerous choking. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T1#GNS324_U5_T1_h4)

question: Why do many women end up turning to dangerous, clandestine abortion methods?

options.A: A personal preference for traditional herbal treatments over hospitals
options.B: Mandatory government programs requiring family planning compliance
options.C: Restrictive laws, social stigma, and poor access to contraception
options.D: Abundant availability of safe surgical clinics in rural areas

explanation: It's all about barriers! When society judges harshly and legal or financial access to safe care is blocked, desperate situations drive people toward risky alternatives. Understanding this helps us practice with empathy, not judgment. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T002#GNS226_U5_T002_h1)

question: What is the main feature of an ergonomic workplace injury?

options.A: It results only from extreme cold temperatures
options.B: It develops slowly over time from repeated physical strain
options.C: It is caused by breathing in airborne bacteria
options.D: It happens instantly from an explosion or spill

explanation: Ergonomic injuries like carpal tunnel or back strain build up gradually when our bodies are subjected to poor posture and repetitive movements. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T5#GNS225_U7_T5_h5)

question: What do macroeconomic indicators provide for a country?

options.A: A numerical snapshot of economic health
options.B: A count of registered nurses
options.C: Individual patient health records
options.D: Hospital room occupancy rates

explanation: Macroeconomic indicators give a broad numerical summary of how a nation's economy is performing overall. [learn more](GST322_U3_T1#GST322_U3_T1_h1)

question: What is the leading cause of heavy bleeding right after childbirth (early postpartum hemorrhage)?

options.A: High blood pressure
options.B: Excessive walking
options.C: Vitamin deficiency
options.D: Uterine atony

explanation: Uterine atony simply means the womb muscle is too tired to clamp down tightly after delivery. Keeping it firm is a key part of your nursing care! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T52#GNS214_U1_T52_h6)

question: What is the standard adult dose and timing for Epinephrine during cardiac arrest?

options.A: 5 mg every 1 minute
options.B: 0.5 mg once only
options.C: 10 mg every 10 minutes
options.D: 1 mg every 3 to 5 minutes

explanation: Giving 1 mg of epinephrine every 3 to 5 minutes keeps blood vessels narrowed to support vital organ perfusion. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T4#GNS315_U4_T4_h5)

question: Why is it so important for a nurse to ask patients about herbal supplements during a medication history?

options.A: Herbal remedies cannot cause any harm or adverse reactions.
options.B: Supplements are strictly regulated by the government for safety.
options.C: Herbal products and supplements can also trigger idiosyncratic reactions.
options.D: Patients only take herbal supplements when prescription drugs fail.

explanation: Never underestimate herbs! Traditional supplements contain active chemicals just like prescription drugs, meaning they can cause unexpected reactions too. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T9#GNS125_U5_T9_h5)

question: What major problem does the Incident Command System prevent when multiple agencies respond to a disaster?

options.A: Shortages of basic food items in grocery stores
options.B: Patients refusing to take their prescribed emergency medications
options.C: Confusion over authority and duplicated efforts among responding groups
options.D: The physical destruction of hospital buildings by storms

explanation: Exactly! Without ICS, different teams might bump heads or waste time doing the exact same job. It keeps everyone organized! [learn more](GNS315_U1_T4#GNS315_U1_T4_h7)

question: Long ago, during the demonological era, what did people generally believe caused mental illness?

options.A: Demonic possession and evil spirits
options.B: Severe vitamin deficiencies
options.C: Chemical imbalances in the brain
options.D: Hereditary genetic mutations

explanation: Before medical science grew, people didn't understand mental health issues yet, so they blamed unusual behaviors on spirits or supernatural forces. You've got this! [learn more](GNS314_U1_T4#GNS314_U1_T4_h1)

question: When assessing a patient's supplement use, which detail is MOST important to record?

options.A: The color and shape of the retail cardboard packaging
options.B: The political affiliation of the supplement manufacturer
options.C: The exact product name, dosage, and frequency of intake
options.D: The name of the transport vehicle used to deliver the pills

explanation: Knowing the exact name and dose helps you and the medical team spot potential drug clashes right away. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T014#GNS227_U7_T014_h6)

question: What is the main difference between bacterial and viral STIs in the body?

options.A: Bacterial infections cause permanent cellular mutations, while viral infections do not
options.B: Viral infections remain in the body long-term, while bacterial infections are usually cured
options.C: Viral infections never respond to any form of pharmaceutical treatment
options.D: Bacterial infections require lifelong maintenance therapy instead of short courses

explanation: Spot on! Bacteria can usually be kicked out with medications, but viruses like HIV or herpes stay in the body for life and need long-term management. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T5#GNS216_U5_T5_h2)

question: Why do local clinics often struggle right after a disaster hits?

options.A: Nurses in local clinics are legally forbidden from treating disaster victims
options.B: They usually lack sufficient resources and capacity to manage sudden mass casualties
options.C: National agencies immediately close local clinics during emergencies
options.D: Community members prefer to travel abroad for emergency care

explanation: Spot on! Primary health centers usually have limited daily supplies, so a sudden influx of injured people can easily overwhelm them. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T12#GNS315_U1_T12_h1)

question: What is the main goal of Primary Health Care (PHC) in a community?

options.A: Providing universally accessible and affordable essential health services
options.B: Focusing exclusively on surgical interventions for chronic illnesses
options.C: Building specialized tertiary hospitals in every local government area
options.D: Training only high-level medical consultants for village clinics

explanation: Think of PHC as bringing basic, affordable health care right to the doorsteps of the people who need it most. You've got this! [learn more](GNS124_U1_T1#GNS124_U1_T1_h1)

question: When is the best time to start planning for a patient's discharge home?

options.A: When the client asks to go home
options.B: After all therapy sessions have finished
options.C: Twenty-four hours before leaving the hospital
options.D: On the day of admission

explanation: Discharge planning starts right from day one! That way, there's no last-minute panic when it's time to go home. Smart nursing! [learn more](GNS314_U5_T2#GNS314_U5_T2_h6)
